spec.title: PROP-059 — User applications: install, launch, alternatives, storage libraries

status.comment: Clean contract adopted 2026-10-30 after the October prototype was archived (branch archive/app-overlay-prototype-2026-10). Implementation follows the APP-CLEAN campaign plan.

p.purpose: vibe is also a small cross-platform meta-distribution: a package of kind `app` describes how to install an upstream application on each supported platform, how to launch it, and which commands it puts on PATH. Several versions or providers of one application may be installed side by side; one is the global default and any shell may pick another for itself. Installed applications live in one or more storage libraries and may be moved between them.

p.principle: The implementation is as simple as the ordinary filesystem allows and no simpler. Durable state is plain files replaced atomically (write a sibling, rename over). There are no journals, checkpoints, leases, seals, witnesses, byte budgets or cold-recovery machinery. An operation interrupted half-way leaves at most an orphan directory, which `vibe storage gc` reports and removes. Missing storage is reported as unavailable, never repaired or guessed around.

p.library-first: Every capability below lives in the `vibe-app` library crate; the CLI, the PATH proxy and any future surface are thin callers (`spec://org.vibevm.world/omnichannel/flows/omnichannel/OMNICHANNEL-PROTOCOL#root`).

p.declaration: An app package has `[package] kind = "app"` and no `[project]` table. `[application]` carries `id` (the slot name, a portable token) and optional `portable` (default `true`). Installation choices live only in `[[installer_options]]`; a package with none is a valid product that `vibe install -g` refuses as not globally installable. Package-author names, never heuristics, supply displayed platform and installer names. The retired fields `installer_package`, `runtime`, `entry`, `commands`, `distribution` and the `[application_source]` table are no longer parsed.

p.installer-options: Each `[[installer_options]]` row has a stable `id`, a human `name`, `platform` id with `platform_name`, `arch` id with optional `arch_name`, optional `portable` override, optional `pre_install` / `post_install` commands, exactly one `installation` method, its `launchers` and its `public_commands`. Predefined platform ids `linux`, `windows`, `macos` and the host CPU architecture are auto-detected; other ids are selectable only explicitly. `vibe install -g` accepts `--platform`, `--arch`, `--installer`; an attended terminal asks platform, then architecture, then installer with the detected row first; an unattended ambiguity is a selection error. `vibe app installers PACKAGE --json` lists every row without installing.

p.installer-separation: `installation.type` is one of `shell`, `zip`, `tar_gz`, `exe`, `msi`, `source_build`; each is the short spelling of a one- or two-step list under `spec://org.vibevm.core/vibevm/common/PROP-065#sugar`, and an option may declare `[[steps]]` directly instead (`PROP-065#steps`). Shell: authored `install`, `force_install`, `uninstall`, `force_uninstall`, optional `update`, `app_root`, and optional `interpreter` (`posix_sh`, `windows_cmd`, `windows_powershell`; host default `posix_sh` on Linux/macOS, `windows_cmd` on Windows). Apt, Homebrew and Winget are shell commands, not kinds. Zip / tar_gz: `source` URL or package-relative path, `sha256`, optional `payload_root`. Exe / msi: `source`, `sha256`, `app_root`, `arguments`, optional `force_arguments`, `uninstall`, `force_uninstall`; they run only on Windows, EXE directly and MSI through `msiexec`. Source_build: `#source-build`. Shell, exe and msi installations are external: vibe records their `app_root` but never deletes or moves it. Zip, tar_gz and source_build installations are owned: vibe places the payload in a library directory it fully controls.

p.launch-points: Each `[[installer_options.launchers]]` row has a stable `id`, `name`, `executable` template, a required `kind` — `gui` (a window of its own), `tui` (a full-screen terminal program, opened by a graphical client through a terminal it starts) or `command` (a console program that reads arguments and prints) — declared by the package author and never inferred, optional `description`, `args`, `working_directory`, `icon` (a path or the icon set of `#menu`), `categories`, `keywords`, booleans `menu` (`#menu`), `terminal` and `default` (at most one default per option). `terminal` is derived from the kind (`true` for `tui` and `command`, `false` for `gui`); when spelled, it must agree, and `vibe check` refuses a disagreement. `[[installer_options.public_commands]]` rows map a PATH command `name` to a launcher `id` of the same option; a command name starts with a lowercase letter or digit and continues with letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.` or `+` (`g++`, `python3.12`), never `vibe`.

p.menu: A graphical client builds a start menu and a taskbar from installed applications, and every entry in it is the package author's explicit decision. A launcher carries `menu = true` to appear there; the default is `false` for every launcher of every kind, so a package shipping a hundred executables lists none of them until the author chooses — a suite of ten utilities and one central program lists the central one, the rest stay installed and reachable through `app launchers`, `app start` and PATH. `[application] menu_group` is the human-readable name of the group the client shows this application's entries under (the way "Adobe Master Collection" is a group), independent of the package name and distinct from `description`; without it, each entry stands alone. `categories` (the freedesktop main categories: `AudioVideo`, `Audio`, `Video`, `Development`, `Education`, `Game`, `Graphics`, `Network`, `Office`, `Science`, `Settings`, `System`, `Utility`) and `keywords` may be set on `[application]` as defaults and on a launcher as its own. An icon is one package-relative path (a PNG or SVG, the short form) or an icon set: `{ svg = "…", png = { "16" = "…", "32" = "…", "48" = "…", "128" = "…", "256" = "…", "512" = "…" }, ico = "…", icns = "…", symbolic = "…", maskable = true }` — `svg` the scalable source, `png` rasters by pixel size, `ico` and `icns` ready containers, `symbolic` a monochrome variant for taskbars, trays and dark surfaces, `maskable` stating the content sits in the central 80% so a platform mask may be applied. Sizes are pixels; `@2x` and DPI scale are the client's concern, which picks the smallest raster not smaller than what it needs. A launcher's icon set overrides the application's; a client falls back from the launcher to the application to its own icon by `kind`. `vibe check` verifies that every named file exists in the package tree, that a PNG is square and matches the size it is listed under (from the header), and that a launcher with `menu = true` has at least an SVG or a PNG of 256 pixels or more; other launchers may have no icon. `describe`, `app list --json` and `app launchers --json` carry `kind`, `menu`, `menu_group`, `categories`, `keywords` and the icon set with resolved absolute paths; `vibe app launchers --all [--menu] --json` lists every ready, exposed installation of the home in one answer, `--menu` only the entries opted in; `vibe app icon PKG [--launcher ID] --size N [--prefer png|svg|symbolic|ico|icns]` prints the path of the best existing file for that size (the smallest raster not smaller than N, else the largest, else the SVG) and never rasterises. Writing system `.desktop`, `.lnk` or icon-theme files is not part of this; it is a later, separate option. Reading them is (`#desktop-entries`).

p.desktop-entries: The launcher model is a superset of a freedesktop desktop entry, so software that ships `.desktop` files is described once. Beyond `#menu`, a launcher may carry `generic_name` (the entry's `GenericName`, "Text editor"), `names` and `descriptions` tables keyed by language tag for localised `Name[xx]` and `Comment[xx]`, `window_class` (`StartupWMClass`, how a taskbar matches windows to the entry), `mime_types` (`MimeType`), and `[[installer_options.launchers.actions]]` rows (`[Desktop Action …]`, a jump list: `id`, `name`, `args`, optional `icon`). The `args` template accepts the placeholders `{file}`, `{files}`, `{url}` and `{urls}` for what a client opens with the launcher (`%f`, `%F`, `%u`, `%U`); `%i`, `%c` and `%k` have no counterpart and are dropped. An installer option may declare `launchers_from = ["share/applications/*.desktop"]`, globs relative to the application root: after the payload is in place, vibe reads every matching file that is an `Application` entry and not `Hidden`, and derives one launcher per file — `id` the file name without `.desktop`, `name`, `generic_name`, `description`, localised tables, `executable` and `args` from `Exec` (the first word resolved through the payload's `bin` and the PATH the launcher will have, field codes mapped as above), `working_directory` from `Path`, `kind` `tui` when `Terminal=true` else `gui`, `categories`, `keywords`, `mime_types`, `window_class`, `actions`, `menu` set to the opposite of `NoDisplay` (the author who ships the entry has decided it is shown), and the icon set from `Icon`: a path is taken as is, a theme name is collected from `share/icons/hicolor/<N>x<N>/apps/<name>.png`, `scalable/apps/<name>.svg` and `symbolic/apps/<name>-symbolic.svg` under the application root. `TryExec`, `StartupNotify`, `OnlyShowIn`, `NotShowIn`, `DBusActivatable` and `X-` keys are ignored. An authored `[[installer_options.launchers]]` row with the same `id` overrides field by field; the derived rows are recorded in the index like authored ones and `app launchers --json` marks each with `source: "authored" | "desktop-entry"`. `vibe app import-desktop FILE…` prints the same rows as manifest TOML for an author who prefers explicit text. The same key vocabulary is the natural target for Windows and macOS metadata later; nothing here is Linux-only except the derivation globs.

p.launcher-paths: Templates accept only `$app_root`, `$app_bin` (`$app_root/bin`), `$project_root` and `$vibe_home`, braced or unbraced, with `$$` for a literal dollar; expansion is one pass, never shell evaluation. A relative executable or icon resolves under `app_root`; a parent traversal, an absolute literal path, or a target outside `app_root` is refused. A working directory may resolve under `app_root` or under the selected project root; without a project, a `$project_root` point reports `requires_project` and the others stay runnable.

p.source-build: `type = "source_build"` declares zero or more `[[installation.sources]]` and one `installation.recipe`; with no sources the package tree itself is the input. Each source has a `name` (directory name), either `url` or package-relative `path`, `sha256`, and `extract` (default `true` for `.zip`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`; otherwise the file is kept under its own filename). The recipe has `interpreter` (as for shell) and `script`, a package-relative file. vibe fetches and verifies every source, caches downloads under the settings root at `cache/app-sources/<sha256>/`, lays them out as `<work>/sources/<name>/`, then runs the script with working directory `<work>` and environment `VIBE_SOURCES`, `VIBE_WORK`, `VIBE_OUT`, `VIBE_PACKAGE` (the package tree) and `VIBE_PLATFORM` / `VIBE_ARCH`. A zero exit with a non-empty `VIBE_OUT` directory makes `VIBE_OUT` the installed payload. `VIBE_OUT` is a staging path: the payload is moved into a library afterwards and may be moved again, so a recipe must produce a relocatable tree (relative lookup or a wrapper) and never bake the staging prefix into it; anything else fails before publication and leaves the work directory for inspection under `cache/app-build/`. `--offline` succeeds only when every source is cached.

p.storage-libraries: A library is a directory holding `vibe-library.toml` (`id`, `created`) and `apps/<slot>/<group>.<name>@<version>/` installation directories. The default library is `<settings>/opt` with id `default` and is created on first use. Additional libraries are listed in `<settings>/storage.toml` as `[[library]]` rows with `id` and absolute `path`; `vibe storage add PATH [--id ID]` creates and lists a fresh one, `attach PATH` lists an existing one whose marker id is not already configured, `detach ID` unlists without deleting, `list` shows each library with its availability and its installations. The default library cannot be detached.

p.availability: A library is available when its path is a directory whose `vibe-library.toml` carries the configured id. Availability is observed at the moment of use, never cached. An installation whose library is unavailable is listed as `unavailable` with the reason, its launchers and PATH proxies report the same reason and exit non-zero, and it is never uninstalled, moved or silently replaced as default; attaching the library again makes it ready without any further command.

p.portability: An owned installation is portable unless `[application].portable = false` or the selected option sets `portable = false`; the effective value is stored in its index record. External installations are never portable.

p.move: `vibe storage move KEY --to LIBRARY` relocates one portable owned installation: copy the directory into the destination library under a temporary name, rename it into place, rewrite the index record, then delete the source directory. A failure before the index rewrite leaves the source untouched and the destination copy an orphan; a failure after it leaves the source directory an orphan. `vibe storage gc` lists and, with `--delete`, removes directories under any available library's `apps/` that no index record references. Moving a non-portable, external or unavailable installation is refused before any copy.

p.index: `<settings>/applications/index.json` (`vibe-user-applications/3`) is the one inventory. It maps installation keys `group/name@version` to records holding the slot, package coordinate, selected option id / platform / architecture, method, `library` id and relative `directory` for owned installations or absolute `app_root` for external ones, the effective portable flag, the authored launchers and public commands, and the authored commands needed later (uninstall, force_uninstall, update, interpreter). It maps slots to their `default` installation key. The file is rewritten atomically under the existing settings lock; a failed operation never replaces a ready record.

p.ownership: The index is the only durable truth; `app_root` of an owned installation is derived from its library and directory at every use. Vibe deletes only directories it owns. A registered external `app_root` is used for launcher resolution and never recursively removed.

p.commands: `vibe install -g PACKAGE`, `vibe update -g PACKAGE` and `vibe uninstall -g PACKAGE` (long form `--global`) operate on one fully qualified app package in the current user's settings root, before and without any project preparation. `install -g` and `update -g` accept `--library ID` for owned methods and refuse it for external ones. A second installation of the same key replaces it in place; a different version of the same slot is added beside the existing ones. `update -g` resolves the newest matching version: an owned method installs it as a new installation and makes it the slot default when the previous default belonged to the same package; a shell method runs the authored `update` command in place. `uninstall -g` removes exactly one key: owned payload directories are deleted, external methods run the authored `uninstall`; if the removed key was the slot default, the default becomes the only remaining ready installation of that slot or `null`, and the command says which.

p.force-and-hooks: `pre_install` runs before the installer and `post_install` after it succeeds, both before the index is written (as steps: a leading `prepare` and a leading `finish` shell step, `PROP-065#steps`); a failing pre-hook stops before installation, a failing post-hook leaves the previous record and restores a previously placed owned payload. `--force` on install or update selects shell `force_install` or exe/msi `force_arguments`, lets an owned payload replace a directory that no index record owns, and is refused for a native method without forced arguments. `--force` on uninstall selects `force_uninstall` of an external method and is refused when none is authored; an owned installation is deleted by ordinary uninstall whatever its contents, so `--force` changes nothing for it. vibe never hashes or re-verifies an installed payload: an owned directory is trusted until it is uninstalled or replaced.

p.child-output: Installer, hook and recipe children inherit stdin and stream stdout and stderr live; in `--json` mode child stdout is relayed to stderr so the JSON envelope stays clean. The child's exit status decides success. Every installer and hook child receives `VIBE_APP_ROOT` (the installation's `app_root`); recipe children receive the variables in `#source-build`; vibe adds nothing else to the environment.

p.launcher-operations: `vibe app launchers PACKAGE --json` lists the launch points of one installation with their resolved availability. `vibe app run PACKAGE LAUNCHER [-- ARGS]` runs one point; `vibe app start PACKAGE [--launcher ID]` runs the explicit default, otherwise asks in an attended terminal and reports `selection_required` unattended. Launch resolves the template, invokes the native program with an argument array and preserves its exit status. `vibe app list` shows every installation with status and slot default.

p.alternatives: `[application].id` names a slot; every installation of that slot is a provider. Each slot has one global default. `vibe app use SLOT KEY` changes it; `vibe app alternatives SLOT` lists providers, the default and the commands each provides. Public commands of all providers in a slot are reserved for that slot; two slots may not claim the same command name. Installing the first provider of a slot makes it the default.

p.proxy: For every reserved command, `<settings>/opt/bin/<command>` (`.exe` on Windows) is a copy of the small native `vibe-app-proxy` binary. Invoked, it locates its home as the nearest ancestor of its own directory that holds `applications/index.json`, reads that index and `storage.toml`, picks the provider from `VIBE_APP_USE` (`slot=key;slot=key`) or the slot default, resolves that provider's launcher for its own command name, and executes the native program directly, forwarding arguments, exit status and, on POSIX, signals. It never runs the vibe CLI. A provider that lacks the command, an unavailable library or an absent default is a clear error with exit 127. Proxies are rewritten whenever the reserved command set changes.

p.hidden-installations: An installation may be hidden: `vibe install -g PKG --hidden` (and `vibe install PKG --hidden` in a project) performs the whole installation — payload in a library, record in the index, movable with `storage move`, updated and uninstalled like any other — but exposes nothing: no proxy in `opt/bin`, no place among the slot's alternatives, never the default. Consent, warnings and installer execution are unchanged; only exposure is withheld. `vibe app expose PKG` turns a hidden installation into an exposed one under the ordinary slot rules (an occupied slot gains an alternative, the default is not taken over); `vibe app hide PKG` is the reverse and releases the default to the next alternative when it held it. `vibe shell --with PKG[@req]` exposes a hidden installation on that session's PATH only, through `#session-selection`. `vibe app update` keeps the hidden state. `vibe app list` lists hidden installations in their own section, and `--json` carries `hidden = true`. A step requirement with build scope (PROP-065 `#app-dependencies`) is exactly a hidden installation made on a package's behalf.

p.session-selection: A session choice is the environment variable `VIBE_APP_USE`; it changes nothing in the index, the slots or `opt/bin`. Reaching an installation that has no proxy there — a hidden one through `--with`, or a build requirement on a step's PATH — needs a proxy somewhere, so vibe keeps those copies under `<home>/cache/app-proxies/<installation>/bin`, a cache like any other: rebuilt on demand, deletable at any time, never consulted by `app list` or the alternatives. `vibe shell` sets it from `--use SLOT=KEY` arguments, so two shells may run different providers of one slot concurrently while the global default stays untouched.

p.shell-command: `vibe shell [-g|--global] [--use SLOT=KEY]...` starts an interactive shell whose PATH begins with the `opt/bin` directories of the selected application homes in priority order: the project home `vibevm/vibeopt` when the working directory is a project and that home exists, then the user settings root and whose `VIBE_APP_USE` reflects the given choices. The shell executable is the caller's parent shell when it is `bash`, `zsh`, `cmd.exe`, `powershell.exe` or `pwsh.exe`, otherwise `/bin/sh` on Linux, `/bin/zsh` on macOS and the system `cmd.exe` on Windows. The command requires an attended non-JSON terminal, preserves the working directory and standard streams, and returns the shell's exit status. `-g` selects the user home alone (`#project-scope`).

p.project-scope: An application may also be installed into a project. `vibe install PACKAGE` without `-g`, run inside a project on a package of kind `app`, records the dependency in `vibe.toml` and `vibe.lock` like any other package and installs it into the project home `vibevm/vibeopt/`, which has exactly the layout of the user home: `applications/index.json`, the default library `opt/` and the proxies in `opt/bin/`; `storage.toml`, extra libraries and `vibe storage` commands apply only to the user home. `vibe install` with no arguments materialises the project's app dependencies the same way, consent-gated because installers run package-authored scripts. `vibe update`, `vibe uninstall` and `vibe app` without `-g` act on the project home when the current directory is inside a project, otherwise on the user home. `vibe shell` in `Auto` scope puts the project home's `opt/bin` before the user home's; `-g` selects the user home alone. `vibevm/vibeopt/` is ignored by git: the lockfile is the record, the directory is a materialisation. External methods installed from a project still register their system-wide `app_root` and are listed as external.

p.acceptance: The gate for every method and command is one public CLI fixture under an isolated settings root: install → list → launch through `app run` and through the PATH proxy → alternatives switch → uninstall. Source_build is proven with a package-local script and two sources (one URL served locally, one package-local file). Storage is proven with two libraries: install into the second, detach, observe `unavailable`, attach, move to the default, `gc` after a simulated interruption. Shell is proven on Linux in a pseudo-terminal. Windows and macOS behaviour is proven on the owner's native machines with the manual tests under `vibevm/vibespecs/manual-tests/`, not by cross-compilation.

p.decisions: Decision: plain files and atomic rename instead of transactional journals. Why: the October prototype grew to 350k lines and an uninstall read 187 GB while chasing crash-proof publication; the owner's requirement was "report a missing disk", not survive it transactionally. Rejected: journals with recovery (unbounded proof cost), a separate build lifecycle for recipes (couples applications to the project build planes). Revisit when a real user loses installation state to an interruption that `storage gc` cannot explain.

p.changelog: 2026-10-31: added `#menu` (explicit `kind`, `menu` opt-in, `menu_group`, categories and keywords, icon sets, `app launchers --all`, `app icon`) and `#desktop-entries` (the launcher model as a superset of freedesktop entries, `launchers_from` derivation, `import-desktop`) on the owner's decisions for the desktop client. 2026-10-31: `#session-selection` names the proxy cache a `--with` session and a build requirement use. 2026-10-31: `#installer-separation` and `#force-and-hooks` point at PROP-065, which generalises a method into a step list, and PROP-064, which adds the `agent` step. 2026-10-31: `#shell-command` names the project home now that `#project-scope` is implemented. 2026-10-31: `#source-build` admits zero sources and states that `VIBE_OUT` is a staging path (first real build: Vim baked its prefix in). 2026-10-30: added `#project-scope` (owner decision the same day). 2026-10-30: rewritten as the clean contract; storage libraries, portability, source builds, session selection by environment and `vibe shell` folded into this document. Retired anchors below keep their names as tombstones. 2026-10-31: added `#hidden-installations` (install without exposing; expose/hide; `shell --with`).

p.sources: Retired 2026-10-19 with the source-versus-binary model. See `#installer-separation` and `#source-build`.

p.distribution: Retired 2026-10-19 with the release-index model. See `#installer-separation`.

p.local-source-shorthand: Retired 2026-10-19. `--registry PATH` remains the way to install from a local registry.

p.context: Retired 2026-10-19 with the installer child-process protocol. See `#installer-separation`.

p.reply: Retired 2026-10-19 with the installer child-process protocol. See `#index`.
